clue.text: Priest taking care of dance

parts.note: a flamen was a priest of ancient Rome serving one god
c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: A clergyman looks after a dancing event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' is only a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is a fiery Spanish style of dance from Andalusia.

clue.text: Port upset couple in House of Lords

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the whole assembly is turned upside down, read bottom to top
in places the pair word inside the abbreviation for the upper chamber

parts.note: HL is the standard abbreviation for the House of Lords
to couple is to tie or join

explanation.surface: A pair of peers fall out in the Lords chamber over a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns the whole assembly, not just the couple; Leith is Edinburgh's port.
explanation.definitionFit: Leith is the historic harbour district of Edinburgh in Scotland.

clue.text: People entertaining girl at the pictures see The Magician

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them within, so the people word holds the rest

parts.note: men means people, as in 'officers and men'
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
the pictures is an everyday British phrase for the cinema

explanation.surface: A group of people take a girl to the cinema to watch a film called The Magician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' and 'see' are only links; the pictures is British slang for the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine man is a tribal healer credited with magical powers, a kind of magician.

clue.text: Transfusion resulting from recruitment drive?

parts.note: a transfusion literally supplies fresh blood, and a hiring campaign figuratively brings fresh people into an organisation

explanation.surface: A blood donation that comes from a hiring campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh recruits to a group are idiomatically called its fresh blood, punning on a transfusion.

clue.text: Cock-a hoop at the North Pole?

definitions.meaning: the North Pole sits literally at the very top of the globe

explanation.definitionFit: Being elated is idiomatically being on the summit of the globe, which the Pole literally is.

clue.text: One managing to bear with poet

indicators.note: to bear something is to carry it, so the manager word carries the letter inside

parts.note: someone who manages or copes is a coper

explanation.surface: A capable person puts up with a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: William Cowper was an 18th-century English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: William Cowper was an English poet and hymn writer of the 1700s.

clue.text: An element of PC

definitions.meaning: a chemical element, the reddish metal with symbol Cu
PC means police constable, colloquially called a cop

explanation.definitionFit: The metal Cu is a chemical element, and British slang calls a police constable by the same word.

clue.text: Yarn cut short in court

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: wool is yarn spun from fleece

explanation.surface: Some thread is trimmed in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' is the verb, to woo, not a law court; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to woo them, seeking their love.

clue.text: Egg on train when temperature becomes cold

indicators.note: becomes signals that one letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: a train of followers is an entourage
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Urging a train along when the weather turns chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' is a link; T in ENTOURAGE changes to C.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge or spur them, a synonym for the answer.

clue.text: Mould could make me wild

indicators.note: could make says the letters can be rearranged to form another word

explanation.surface: A fungus growth that drives someone crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildew is a thin whitish mould that grows on plants and damp surfaces.

clue.text: Highest score — excellent!

definitions.meaning: a notch is a score or tally mark, so the uppermost mark
an exclamation of approval meaning first-rate

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means first-rate, literally the uppermost scored mark on a tally stick.

clue.text: Smart child discards king

indicators.note: discards means the letter for the monarch is thrown out

parts.note: chick is an affectionate word for a child
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A well-dressed youngster gets rid of a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish, elegant, smart in appearance.

clue.text: He helps Irish housewife clean up her mess

indicators.note: mess as a verb means jumble, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An Irish home help tidies up after a messy housewife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' looks like a noun belonging to the housewife but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish folklore has small sprites who secretly help with household work, as brownies do.

clue.text: Chatelaine would take temporary responsibility

parts.note: a chatelaine is mistress of a castle, so she would literally keep the castle while others are away

explanation.surface: The lady of the castle steps in for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to take charge temporarily, literally to keep a stronghold in safe hands.

clue.text: Deadlock man attached to shed

indicators.note: attached to joins the two pieces in order, name first

parts.note: Stan is a man's name
to doff a hat is to shed or take it off

explanation.surface: A fellow connected to a garden shed is stuck in a deadlock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a garden hut but is the verb, to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-off is a deadlock in which neither side gives way.

clue.text: Hedge where gold is found in valley

indicators.note: found in places gold and is inside the valley

parts.note: Tempe is a famous valley in Thessaly, Greece
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Gold can be discovered in a river valley hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vale of Tempe is a celebrated gorge in Greece; 'where' is only a link, and 'Hedge' is the verb meaning to stall.
explanation.definitionFit: To hedge is to stall or avoid committing oneself, which is what temporising means.

clue.text: Start van

definitions.meaning: a head start, as in having a ... of ten metres
the van or vanguard is the front position

explanation.definitionFit: A lead is both an advantage at the start and the front position, the van.

clue.text: Mother has to dress up little boy showing glee

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to gird is to dress or equip oneself
Al is a short form of a boy's name like Alan

explanation.surface: A mother must clothe her young son, who is full of glee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glee' is a part-song for unaccompanied voices, not happiness; 'up' turns GIRD into DRIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A glee is an unaccompanied part-song, as is a madrigal.

clue.text: I am a male religious leader

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm, written IM

explanation.surface: Someone introducing himself as a man of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am' is shortened to I'M; then A as written and M for male.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque, a Muslim religious leader.

clue.text: Listen to the row becoming less restrained

parts.note: to listen is to hear
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Hearing an argument that gets more unrestrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but is a line of seats; 'to the' and 'becoming' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartier means more vigorous and unrestrained, as in a heartier laugh.

clue.text: Malfunction of arc light, flickering when deprived of argon

indicators.note: flickering suggests the letters shift about into a new order

parts.note: Ar is the chemical symbol for argon

explanation.surface: A faulty arc lamp flickers when its argon runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When deprived of' tells you the argon letters leave the lamp phrase, and the remaining six letters are then shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a sudden minor malfunction or fault.

clue.text: Bluebottle has to glide into a place from which escape is difficult

indicators.note: into places the gliding word inside the place word

parts.words: a place from which escape is difficult
parts.note: being in a tight corner means being trapped
to flow is to glide smoothly

explanation.surface: A fly glides into a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluebottle' looks like the fly but is a country name for a blue flower; 'has to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebottle is an old country name for the blue cornfield flower.

clue.text: Novel item made without peripherals

indicators.note: without peripherals means the outer letters at both ends are removed, leaving the core

explanation.surface: A new item produced with no add-ons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' is the noun, Jane Austen's book, not 'new'; strip two letters from each end of ITEMMADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a novel by Jane Austen published in 1815.

clue.text: Secondary road heading north followed by soldiers

indicators.note: followed by puts the soldiers after the road and direction pieces

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A minor road heading north, with troops behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a major British motorway; 'heading' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor means secondary or lesser in importance.

clue.text: Knocking back endless wine is ominous

indicators.note: knocking back means the run of letters is read backwards, as one knocks back a drink
endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: retsina is a Greek resinated wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Downing a glass of wine with no end is a bad sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' turns RETSINA into RETSIN; 'Knocking back' turns RETSINIS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means threatening, ominous, suggesting harm ahead.

clue.text: Bad state

definitions.meaning: The abbreviation for Illinois, a US state

explanation.definitionFit: Ill means bad or sick, and it abbreviates the US state of Illinois.

clue.text: Plot crushed

definitions.meaning: a plot of land, a piece of earth
past tense of grind, milled to powder

explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a piece of land, and crushed coffee beans have been milled.

clue.text: This can be achieved by breaking the law

definitions.text: This can be achieved by breaking the law

indicators.note: breaking shatters the words so their letters rearrange

explanation.surface: Riches can come from crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This can be achieved by' points at the answer while 'breaking' scrambles THE LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Riches are what lawbreakers such as robbers seek, so crime can bring abundance.

clue.text: Delaying conversion to idolatry

indicators.note: conversion changes the word's letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Putting off a religious conversion to idol worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory means slow to act, delaying or tardy.
